subject: Admin activity export for SIG / on-demand evidence request
messages:
From: Alyssa Berg <alyssa@auditpartners.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-30 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: admin activity snapshot for SIG on-demand review

Hi Sofia,

MedicaSys's SIG review team needs an on-demand export of administrative activity for the window 2026-06-01 to 2026-08-01. They asked us to confirm the fields you can provide and the delivery options. At minimum they want: actor identifier, action type, timestamp (UTC), resource id/path, IP address, session id, object before/after (when applicable), and a tamper-evident checksum/manifest.

Questions from their checklist:
- Can you include both console/API actions and operator/privileged sessions?
- Do you provide raw session ids or do you pseudonymize user ids for exports?
- What is the default retention and can you export historical slices (we may request a 24-month carve-out)?
- Delivery preferences: S3 presigned + encrypted bundle, SFTP, or direct secure transfer?

I've attached our SIG evidence checklist for reference (audit_questionnaire_SIG.pdf). Please let me know what format/schema you can export (CSV, NDJSON, or compressed Parquet) and any redaction options you support. Also call out any event classes you do NOT include (eg. ephemeral KV-cache hits or internal telemetry).

We aim to catalogue this as part of an on-site review; ETA for initial export would be helpful.

Thanks,
Alyssa Berg
Audit Partner, Audit Partners LLC
alyssa@auditpartners.com

From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.com>
To: Alyssa Berg <alyssa@auditpartners.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-30 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: admin activity snapshot for SIG on-demand review

Hi Alyssa — thanks for the checklist and the clear ask. High-level answers below; we can iterate on scope once you confirm timeframe and filters.

What we log (high level):
- Actor metadata: internal principal id (employee/email), role, and service account ids for machine actors.
- Action classification: create/read/update/delete, login/auth, privilege_grant/revoke, config_change, role_assignment, keystore/access.
- Timestamp: ISO 8601 UTC (we provide both event_time and ingest_time).
- Resource identifiers: canonical resource path and ARN-style id where applicable.
- Network context: source IP, geo (country), user agent string.
- Session context: session_id, request_id, and parent_request_id for traceability.
- Before/after diffs for config and policy changes (where stored by service).

What we do NOT include in admin activity exports by default: ephemeral KV cache hit metrics, internal host telemetry (cpu/mem), and debug-level agent logs. We DO include operator action entries (console, CLI, and API) and privileged session start/stop markers.

Retention and historical slices: default retention for admin activity is 12 months for standard accounts; privileged actions are retained 24 months. We can produce historical slices outside retention if the data is still available in backups or if the customer has an extended retention contract. For MedicaSys we can propose a 24-month carve-out if you confirm the business reason.

Export formats and delivery:
- Formats: NDJSON (line-delimited JSON) is our recommended default for fidelity; CSV for summary-level exports; compressed Parquet for analytics-friendly deliveries.
- Delivery: S3 presigned URL with PGP-encrypted tarball and a signed manifest (SHA256 + HMAC) is our standard for high-sensitivity exports. SFTP and secure HTTPS webhook delivery are also supported.

Redaction and pseudonymization:
- We can produce PII-preserved exports (full actor ids) or hashed/pseudonymized actor ids (salted SHA256) if requested.
- Field-level redaction rules can be applied before export (PII, email addresses, IPs) — note this makes some traceability queries harder for the auditor.

Estimates and next steps:
- Rough compressed size for a 2-month window for a mid-sized tenant is ~8–15GB depending on sampling and include-diffs.
- We will provide an export_schema_v1.csv describing the column names and example rows.
- To proceed: confirm exact time window, desired format, redaction level, and preferred delivery method. Also let us know if you need a signed chain-of-custody manifest and whether you require HSM-backed timestamps.

I'll attach the draft export schema and a short checklist for the transfer. If you want, we can schedule a short 30-minute call to lock scope and timeline.

Thanks,
Sofia Ivanova
Manager, Trust & Security — Redwood Inference
sofia_ivanova@redwood.com

Attachment: export_schema_v1.csv (CSV, 6KB)
From: Alyssa Berg <alyssa@auditpartners.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-30 13:48:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: admin activity snapshot for SIG on-demand review

Thanks, Sofia — that is really helpful. A couple of clarifying notes from the MedicaSys team:

1) Time window: they actually want 2024-08-01 through 2026-07-31 (24 months). Please confirm whether the 24-month carve-out is possible and whether there are any egress cost implications.
2) Actor identifiers: they want direct principal identifiers for correlation to their HR roster — pseudonymization is acceptable only if you provide a reversible mapping under an HSM escrow process.
3) KV-cache events: they asked specifically whether prefix/KV caching summaries are included as admin activity or only as telemetry. If they are telemetry-only, they'll want a separate sampling.
4) Chain-of-custody: they require a signed manifest with per-file SHA256 and a high-assurance signature (PGP or x509) plus an attested delivery timestamp.

Can you confirm the ETA for a first-pass export if we proceed with S3 presigned + PGP-encrypted tarball, full actor ids (no pseudonymization), and the requested 24-month window? Also please call out any manual steps (legal/PO) that will affect schedule.

Best,
Alyssa

Subject: Re: Request: admin activity snapshot for SIG on-demand review

Hi Alyssa — quick update and proposed timeline:

- 24-month carve-out: we can assemble the requested 2024-08-01 to 2026-07-31 export. There are two caveats: (1) if any parts of that window are beyond the customer's contracted retention we will pull from cold backups which requires an extra validation step (adds one business day), and (2) egress costs will be billed per the standard contract unless MedicaSys requests us to waive them as part of a negotiation.

- Actor identifiers: we can deliver full principal identifiers. For reversible pseudonymization we need an HSM escrow arrangement; let us know if MedicaSys prefers that path.

- KV-cache/prefix caching: those events are recorded in a separate ephemeral telemetry ledger and are NOT included in the default admin activity export. If you need them we can produce a sampled summary (approx 5% of events) or a full extract (extra processing). Please confirm sampling preference.

- Chain-of-custody and manifest: our standard is a PGP-signed manifest + SHA256 per file and an HMAC over the manifest. We can also provide a notarized timestamp (HSM-backed) on request.

ETA for first-pass export: 3 business days after contract handshake and receipt of a signed export request form + delivery details (target S3 bucket and PGP public key). Manual steps: legal must sign the export addendum (we'll route a one-page addendum), and finance must acknowledge potential egress charges if MedicaSys is billed.

I'll attach a short Evidence Export Checklist (evidence_export_checklist_draft.docx) for the MedicaSys procurement team to complete; that form speeds handoff and clarifies billing. If that works I'll schedule the export job and share a preview manifest before transfer.

Thanks,
Sofia
Manager, Trust & Security — Redwood Inference
